rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate all eight peaks and identify critical pairs while limiting late-elution penalties. The observed elution window will guide subsequent window trimming and slope or temperature adjustments.

Halve the gradient slope while keeping the window and temperature fixed to test whether the clustered peaks separate with shallower elution. The first run's early elution leaves room to gain resolution without a large time penalty.

Keep the improved gradient slope and raise temperature to shift selectivity in the remaining unresolved cluster. Higher temperature should also shorten retention, preserving the margin below the 10-minute penalty threshold.

Make the gradient slightly shallower at the best temperature to test separation of the remaining critical pair. The current last peak at 8.56 minutes leaves time for this adjustment without an expected time penalty.

The shallower gradient worsened the critical pair, so test a steeper gradient instead. Reducing tG to 18 minutes should improve that pair and shorten the run, while checking whether the earlier cluster retains adequate resolution.

The best run is nearly fully resolved, but changing slope trades resolution between two critical pairs. Test a modest temperature decrease at the same slope to shift selectivity while retaining ample room below the 10-minute threshold.

Return to 60 C and retain the best run's gradient slope while raising the starting organic fraction slightly. This tests a window-driven selectivity adjustment for the marginal pair and should shorten retention without reaching the final hold.

Slightly reduce the slope from injection 7 to improve the early cluster while preserving its improved separation of the later critical pair. The narrowed window still extends beyond the observed elution window and should keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Reduce the slope slightly from 0.04583 to 0.045 organic fraction per minute to lift the marginal early pairs above R = 1.5. The later critical pair has a small resolution margin, and all peaks should remain within the gradient and below 10 minutes.

Injection 9 has reached the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark while seeking a faster fully resolved method. Raise the starting organic fraction and slightly reduce the slope to offset compression of the early cluster.

Make the gradient shallower at the higher starting organic fraction to recover resolution in the early critical pair. This tests whether the shorter elution window can support full resolution; injection 9 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

The higher-starting-organic trials trade resolution between critical pairs without improving the benchmark. Test the opposite temperature limit using injection 9's gradient to look for a different selectivity pattern that could support subsequent acceleration.

At 25 C, raise the gradient window while retaining the same slope to shorten the run and test starting-composition selectivity for the lone unresolved pair. Injection 9 remains the fully resolved, maximum-score fallback.

The critical pair converged as the starting organic fraction rose; a further shift may carry it through an elution-order reversal and restore separation. Keep the slope fixed to isolate this effect while testing a substantially shorter run.

The critical pair reopened at the higher starting organic fraction, so advance the window one more step at the same slope. This may achieve full resolution faster than injection 9, while the other pairs currently have resolution margins.

Injection 15 achieves the maximum score with all peaks eluting by 4.35 minutes. Shorten the gradient by one step to seek a faster fully resolved method, monitoring the two pairs with the smallest resolution margins.
Back off the gradient steepness by lowering the endpoint one grid step. This intermediate slope should recover the marginal pair while eluting the mixture faster than injection 15.
Raise temperature one step using the fastest fully resolved method so far. This tests whether retention can be shortened further without losing the modest resolution margins in the critical pairs.

Return to 25 C and test a higher, narrower organic window for a faster separation with different selectivity. The shallower slope may preserve resolution, but the first peaks must be checked for excessive compression; injection 17 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Lower the starting organic fraction one step from injection 19 while preserving its shallow slope to recover the unresolved central pair and improve early retention. This intermediate window may still elute all compounds faster than the fully resolved 4.14-minute benchmark.

Trim injection 17's unused gradient tail while preserving its starting composition, temperature, and slope. Its last peak eluted near 0.525 organic fraction, so a 0.55 endpoint should retain full resolution with a shorter programmed gradient.
